patterns.title: A Windows service failed to start or stopped
patterns.summary: The Service Control Manager recorded a failure for the service '{detail}'. A service that is missing, broken or waiting on another service can stop software that depends on it.

remediation.detail: Find out what depends on it and whether the failure is new.
Event 7001 means a service it needs did not start.
The same time in the System log often shows the first thing that went wrong.

patterns.title: An application crashed
patterns.summary: Windows recorded an application crash or hang: {detail}

remediation.detail: The crash entry names the module that failed; a runtime or driver is often the cause.

remediation.action: Check it is the same app Intune installed
remediation.detail: A crash right after install points at a missing prerequisite or a corrupt package.

patterns.title: The device shut down or restarted unexpectedly
patterns.summary: The previous shutdown was not clean (power loss, crash or forced restart). Installs and policy runs that were in progress would have been cut off.

remediation.action: Check what ran at the time
remediation.detail: Compare the time with Intune install and script logs.
More than a one-off points at hardware, drivers or a battery problem.

patterns.title: Disk or file system errors
patterns.summary: Windows logged a disk or file system problem. Failed installs, corrupt downloads and unexplained errors can follow.

remediation.detail: Run a file system check and look at the drive's health.
A full system drive causes many install failures.

patterns.title: A Windows Installer install failed
patterns.summary: The Windows Installer service recorded a failed installation: {detail}

remediation.detail: Re-run the install with verbose logging; this event only says it failed.

remediation.action: Search the MSI log for 'Return value 3'
remediation.detail: The first one is the step that failed.

patterns.title: A Windows update failed to install or download
patterns.summary: The Windows Update client recorded a failure: {detail}

remediation.detail: The code in the event says whether it is a download, servicing or disk problem.
Servicing errors are explained in C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log.

patterns.title: An app package (MSIX/Store) failed to deploy
patterns.summary: The app package deployment service reported a failure: {detail}

remediation.action: Read the error code in the event
remediation.detail: 0x80073CF3 and similar codes name the exact problem (conflict, dependency, disk space).
MSIX apps fail when a required VCLibs or .NET framework package is missing.

patterns.title: Intune/MDM reported an error
patterns.summary: The Windows MDM client (the part of Windows that talks to Intune) logged an error-level event, ID {detail}. Policy or app settings may not have applied.

remediation.detail: Open the event in the DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider Admin log; it names the setting and the error code.
Find the profile or policy that owns the setting named in the event.

patterns.title: BitLocker reported an error
patterns.summary: BitLocker logged an error-level event (ID {detail}). Encryption policies from Intune often fail on missing TPM, Secure Boot or recovery key backup.

patterns.title: Group Policy processing failed
patterns.summary: Group Policy could not be processed, usually because the domain controller or SYSVOL share could not be reached.

remediation.detail: Cloud-only devices can ignore this; hybrid devices need a line of sight to a domain controller.

remediation.action: Check the AppLocker or WDAC policy
remediation.detail: Allow the publisher or path, or confirm the block is intended.

patterns.title: Microsoft Defender detected or blocked something
patterns.summary: Defender recorded a detection: {detail}. If it relates to an installer, Defender may have quarantined files mid-install.

remediation.action: Exclude or re-sign the installer if it is safe
remediation.detail: Quarantined installer files cause exit codes like 2 or 1603.
